item.title: Microsoft Dynamics 365
item.description:
Dynamics 365 combines CRM and ERP in a modular set of cloud applications. The sales and customer service apps manage leads, opportunities, cases, and customer communications, while finance, supply chain, and Business Central handle accounting, inventory, purchasing, and operations. Because the modules share a data platform, a company can start with one and add others over time, and they connect closely with Microsoft 365, Teams, and Power BI.

Copilot is built throughout. In sales, it summarizes accounts and meetings, drafts emails, and suggests next steps. In service, it helps agents find answers and summarize cases, and in finance and supply chain, it supports tasks like reconciliations, collections, and spotting disruptions. AI agents take on routine tasks, such as qualifying leads or processing orders, and Copilot Studio lets companies build their own.

item.title: Conduyt
item.description:
Conduyt takes an approach to CRM pricing that departs from the per-seat model. A team pays a single price no matter how many people use the product, which suits small sales teams and agencies that would otherwise pay for every added user.

The basics are familiar: a contact database, deal pipelines, and activity tracking, with AI features that draft follow-up messages, summarize interactions, and reduce routine data entry. Positioned as AI-native, it aims to have the software do the admin work that salespeople dislike.

item.title: Gainsight
item.description:
Gainsight was one of the first platforms for the customer success discipline. It pulls usage, support, survey, and billing data to produce a health score for every customer, so teams can see who needs attention before a renewal is at risk. Playbooks guide the steps a manager should take for each situation.

AI features predict churn, suggest next actions, summarize account history, and draft communications. Surveys, in-app engagement, and a community product complete the suite, and the company has expanded into customer education. Reports help leaders show the effect of customer success on retention.

item.title: HubSpot CRM
item.description: HubSpot CRM is the shared database underneath every HubSpot product, and it can also be used on its own at no cost. It stores contacts, companies, deals, and tickets, logs emails and calls against each record, and shows a pipeline of deals by stage. Connecting Gmail or Outlook means sent and received messages are attached to the right contact automatically, so people spend less time on manual data entry. For a small business that has been running on spreadsheets, it is an easy first step into a real CRM.

item.title: Pipedrive
item.description: Pipedrive is designed by and for salespeople, with the pipeline at the center. Deals appear as cards that move across stages, from first contact to closed, so reps can see at a glance what needs attention. Each deal has activities, emails, notes, and files attached, and the system reminds you of follow-ups so nothing slips. Compared with big CRM suites, the interface is clean and quick to learn, which suits small and growing sales teams.

item.title: Salesforce
item.description: Salesforce is the CRM that large companies tend to run their sales and customer operations on. It tracks leads, accounts, opportunities, and support cases, and it is sold as separate clouds for Sales, Service, Marketing, and Commerce, with Slack, Tableau, and MuleSoft added for collaboration, analytics, and integration. Underneath is a platform that lets companies build custom objects, workflows, and apps, which is why Salesforce setups can look very different from one company to the next.

item.title: Zoho CRM
item.description:
Zoho CRM covers the normal work of sales: tracking leads and contacts, managing deals through a pipeline, logging calls and emails, and forecasting revenue. It supports multiple channels, including phone, email, live chat, and social media, and lets you build custom modules and fields so it can reflect how a business actually sells. Workflow rules, assignment rules, and blueprints enforce a consistent sales process without manual follow-up.

Zia is the AI layer. It scores leads by how likely they are to convert, predicts which deals will close, spots unusual activity, and recommends the best time to contact a prospect. It can answer questions in plain language, summarize records, and help draft emails. Because Zoho builds its own models, it positions this as a cost-effective alternative to enterprise AI add-ons. Integrations connect with Zoho’s other products such as Campaigns, Books, and Desk, and with outside tools through a marketplace.

item.title: Attio
item.description:
Attio starts from the idea that every company sells differently. Instead of fixed objects like leads and opportunities, teams build their own structures, such as customers, partners, or investors, and link them. The interface feels more like a spreadsheet and a database than a traditional CRM, so it is easier to reshape.

Data fills in with little typing. Attio connects to email and calendar to log interactions, enriches company and contact details, and shows the strength of relationships. AI features summarize accounts, answer questions about the pipeline, and fill in fields from conversations. Workflow automation moves records, sends notifications, and updates data.

item.title: Close
item.description:
Close takes the position that sales reps should do their work from one screen. Calls, emails, and texts happen inside the CRM and are logged automatically, so there is less manual data entry and a complete history on each lead. Power dialers let reps work through lists quickly.

Sequences automate multi-step outreach that mixes email, calls, and texts, and workflows keep pipelines moving. AI features transcribe and summarize calls, suggest follow-ups, and score leads, which helps managers coach and helps reps decide where to spend time. Reporting shows activity and results by rep.

item.title: Copper
item.description:
Copper integrates with the tools its users already work in. Because it lives inside Gmail and connects with Google Calendar, Drive, and Docs, contacts and conversations are logged automatically, so reps do not have to copy information into a separate system.

The CRM covers the usual sales functions: contacts, companies, deals, pipelines, tasks, and reporting. Project management features track work after a deal closes, which suits agencies and service firms. AI features help summarize communication and suggest follow-ups, and workflow automation moves deals through stages.

item.title: Folk
item.description:
Folk is a relationship manager for people who find traditional CRMs heavy. Users import contacts from email, LinkedIn, and spreadsheets, organize them into groups, and track conversations and deals in a clean interface. It suits agencies, recruiters, investors, and founders who manage many relationships.

AI and automation reduce the manual work. Enrichment fills in details like company and role, a browser extension saves profiles from LinkedIn, and sequences send personalized emails at scale. AI helps write messages and summarize history, and reminders prompt follow-ups so nobody falls through the cracks.

item.title: Freshsales
item.description:
Freshsales is a sales CRM that keeps lead and deal information in one view. Teams track contacts, run pipelines, and log calls and emails, with a built-in phone and chat so reps can contact prospects without switching tools. Automation moves leads through stages and assigns tasks.

Freddy AI assists with prioritization. It scores leads by likelihood to convert, predicts which deals will close, and suggests next best actions, while generative features draft emails and summarize conversations. Analytics show pipeline health, and integrations connect with Freshdesk, marketing tools, and common business apps.

item.title: Salesflare
item.description:
Salesflare fills itself in. It connects to email, calendar, and phone, then builds contact and company profiles with conversation history, social data, and notes, so sales reps do not need to type everything. A timeline shows every interaction with a contact.

Features include pipelines, workflows, email tracking, and sequences, plus an intelligent assistant that nudges reps when a lead has gone quiet. It works with Gmail, Outlook, and a mobile app.

item.title: Streak
item.description:
Streak adds pipeline management to Gmail. Users create boxes for deals, candidates, or projects, move them through stages, and see all related emails, notes, and files in one place. Because it sits in the inbox, there is little context switching.

Features include mail merge, email tracking, scheduling, shared inboxes, and automations. AI helps summarize threads and draft emails. It suits small teams that already run on Google Workspace.

Streak has a free plan and paid tiers. It is tied to Gmail. Alternatives include Copper, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Close, and Attio. Streak suits small teams working from the inbox.

item.title: Lightfield
item.description:
Lightfield rethinks the CRM as a system that fills itself. It connects to email, calendar, and call recordings, and extracts contacts, companies, deals, and notes automatically, so records stay current without reps typing. The aim is to remove the data entry that makes CRMs unpopular.

Beyond capturing data, it uses the context to help with work, such as drafting follow-ups, answering questions about accounts, and surfacing deals that need attention. The team behind it previously built Tome, a presentation tool, before turning to this product.
